turns.prompt:
You are given one attached CSV file:
  - cdft_piezo_pool.csv: 100 CANDIDATE crystalline materials whose
    properties are NOT given, columns `candidate_id`, `formula` and `poscar`
    (the crystal structure, in POSCAR format).

No property values are provided. Using your knowledge of crystal chemistry,
crystal symmetry and structure-property relationships, predict which
candidates have the LARGEST piezoelectric strain coefficient max|d_ij| (in
pC/N), then select the 5 best candidates from the pool.

Reason from the structures, then end your answer with an explicit ranked
list of candidate_ids, best first, e.g. "Final: c901, c902, c903, c904,
c905".
turns.answer_text:
The piezoelectric strain tensor \(d_{ij}\) is identically zero in any structure possessing inversion symmetry. Among the non-centrosymmetric candidates the magnitude of \(\max|d_{ij}|\) is controlled by the product of the piezoelectric stress constants \(e_{ij}\) (large when Born charges are anomalous) and the elastic compliances \(s_{kl}\) (large when the lattice is mechanically soft).  

Consequently the highest responses are expected from two families:  
- polar packings of small, highly polar molecules (very small elastic moduli), and  
- lone-pair perovskites or layered iodides (anomalous Born charges plus intrinsically soft lattices).  

Inspection of the supplied POSCARs identifies precisely these motifs:  
- c092 (SF4) and c051 (H3F2) are molecular crystals whose polar molecules occupy a single, inversion-free site;  
- c029 (GeH3Cl) is a polar molecular packing of a pyramidal Ge(IV) species;  
- c041 and c026 are rhombohedrally distorted Ge(II) chloride perovskites (lone-pair ferroelectrics);  
- c047 is a polar, van-der-Waals-layered iodide.  

All other non-centrosymmetric entries (wurtzites, half-Heuslers, oxides, \ldots) are either mechanically stiffer or lack comparably large Born charges and therefore exhibit substantially smaller \(d_{ij}\).  

Final: c092, c047, c051, c029, c041
